fatal_errors: Replacing only 10 at.% of Fe with Cr does not yield an almost equiatomic FeCoNiCr alloy, so the proposed composition does not clearly satisfy the stated high-entropy-alloy qualification.
No supporting observations or citations from earlier work are provided.
The proposed generic Cr-induced exchange and anisotropy changes do not identify a structural mediator or establish why coercivity should increase.
The hypothesis misses the target Ti-enabled fcc/C14 dual-phase intervention and its interface/domain-wall-pinning mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general goal of increasing coercivity in an FeCoNi-derived alloy and supplies a measurable prediction with an explicit falsification threshold. However, it neither reconstructs the FeCoNiTi dual-phase intervention nor its phase-specific magnetic mechanism, temperature range, transitions, or approximately 667 Oe outcome at 400 K. The nominal 10 at.% Cr formulation is not almost equiatomic, and its claimed 20% coercivity increase is arbitrary and unsupported by prior observations. The experiment is somewhat discriminating, but it lacks compositionally and processing-matched controls, structural characterization, temperature-dependent measurements, and tests linking any coercivity change to Cr-mediated exchange or anisotropy.
